Project enrollment forward

Source: R/project-enrollment.R
project_enrollment.Rd

Projects grade-level enrollment forward any number of years with the grade progression ratio method. It builds a projection matrix from ratios and advances enrollment one year at a time (one matrix-vector product per year), replacing the entry grade each year with the value you supply. ratios is optional when you supply a schedule.

Usage

project_enrollment(
  base,
  ratios = NULL,
  horizon = NULL,
  entry = NULL,
  schedule = NULL,
  start_year = NULL
)

Arguments

base

Most recent observed enrollment: either a data frame with columns grade and enrollment (optionally year), or a named numeric vector. Grade values or vector names must be present and unique. Enrollment must be finite, non-missing, and non-negative.

ratios

A data frame or data-frame subclass with columns grade_from, grade_to, and ratio, as returned by progression_ratios(). grade_from and grade_to must not be missing. ratio must be numeric, non-negative, and finite. An infinite ratio (from a feeder grade with zero enrollment) is an error. NA/NaN ratios, for example from sparse history, stay in the matrix with a warning.

horizon

Number of years to project (a positive integer).

entry

Exogenous entry-grade enrollment for each projected year: a numeric vector of length horizon, or a data frame with an enrollment or value column. Values must be finite, non-missing, and non-negative. If NULL, the entry grade stays at its base value, with a warning.

schedule

Optional prebuilt projection schedule: a list of per-year steps, such as one produced by swing_schedule(). See the Schedules section for what a step contains. When supplied, ratios and entry must be NULL, and horizon defaults to the number of steps.

start_year

Optional integer label for the base year; output years start at start_year + 1. It and every resulting year must fit in R's integer range. If NULL, the year comes from base$year when present; that column must hold a single integer value in the same range. Without a year column, output years are 1 to horizon.

Value

A long data frame with columns year, grade, and enrollment, covering the projected years only.

Schedules

Each step is list(matrix = <square projection matrix>, entry = <NULL or a single number>), with an optional total. Each matrix must be numeric and square, and its non-missing coefficients must be finite and non-negative. Row and column names must be unique and identical, in the same order, and every step must use the same names. A step's entry must be NULL or one finite, non-negative number.

A step's total rescales that year's grades, entry grade included, after the entry value is applied. It is either one finite, non-negative school total or "base", the sum of the base grades. The rescaled grades are recorded and carried into the next step. Steps without a total aren't rescaled, so the projection continues from the last rescaled grades with the supplied entry values.

Rescaling needs a finite, positive projected total. A missing or infinite projected total is an error, and so is a positive target on a zero projection. If both the projection and the target are zero, the grades are left as they are. A zero target empties that year, so a later target has only the entry classes that arrive afterwards to rescale.

NA/NaN coefficients are kept, with a warning. A missing coefficient can make its grade missing in the output. If that grade is still missing after the entry value is applied, the next matrix multiplication makes every grade missing, because zero times a missing value is still missing. A non-NULL entry value then restores only the entry grade.

Examples

history <- data.frame(
  year = rep(2021:2023, each = 3),
  grade = factor(rep(c("K", "1", "2"), 3), levels = c("K", "1", "2")),
  enrollment = c(100, 90, 80, 110, 95, 88, 120, 99, 91)
)
ratios <- progression_ratios(history)
base <- subset(history, year == 2023, c("grade", "enrollment"))
project_enrollment(base, ratios,
  horizon = 3, entry = c(125, 130, 128),
  start_year = 2023
)
#>   year grade enrollment
#> 1 2024     K  125.00000
#> 2 2024     1  111.00000
#> 3 2024     2   95.81579
#> 4 2025     K  130.00000
#> 5 2025     1  115.62500
#> 6 2025     2  107.42982
#> 7 2026     K  128.00000
#> 8 2026     1  120.25000
#> 9 2026     2  111.90607
